title: Authentication and Identity
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of authentication and identity in a Swift program or workflow.
Apply authentication versus authorization in a small, inspectable example.
Check the expected result and identify one boundary case or platform constraint.

content.intro: This lesson focuses on authentication and identity and the practical choices around it. Start with the smallest example, connect it to “Authentication versus authorization”, and verify the result before adding complexity.
content.why_it_matters: Application code connects state, UI, APIs, data storage and platform capabilities. Clear ownership and explicit failure states make the experience more reliable and accessible.

content_blocks.title: Application Security Boundaries
content_blocks.alt_text: The diagram shows untrusted input passing through validation and authorization, while diagnostics avoid exposing secrets.
content_blocks.caption: Treat external values and secrets deliberately.

content_blocks.text: **Start with the rule.** Treat input from files, networks, and users as untrusted. Validate at boundaries, enforce authorization server-side, protect credentials, minimize retained data, and redact logs.

**Work through the lesson.** Add real application capabilities with explicit privacy, persistence, platform API, accessibility, localization, and release considerations. The detailed subtopic list in this lesson preserves the curriculum coverage; treat each item as a cue for a small example or a focused question rather than trying to memorize syntax.

items.title: Authentication versus authorization
items.text: Treat input from files, networks, and users as untrusted. Validate at boundaries, enforce authorization server-side, protect credentials, minimize retained data, and redact logs.

items.title: Sign-in flows and session state
items.text: SwiftUI describes the interface as a hierarchy of views derived from state. Keep state ownership clear, compose reusable views, and verify keyboard, accessibility, and size-adaptation behavior.

items.title: Secure token handling concepts
items.text: For secure token handling concepts, separate app behavior from presentation and platform services. Define ownership and error states, test the behavior independently where possible, and verify Apple-platform requirements on a supported target.

items.title: Expired sessions and sign-out behavior
items.text: For expired sessions and sign-out behavior, separate app behavior from presentation and platform services. Define ownership and error states, test the behavior independently where possible, and verify Apple-platform requirements on a supported target.

content_blocks.title: Example: Authentication and Identity
content_blocks.run_instructions: Save a command-line example as main.swift and run `swift main.swift` with an installed compatible Swift toolchain. If the snippet imports SwiftUI, Swift Testing, or platform-only frameworks, use the matching Apple-platform project or Swift package instead. CodeLeaf’s browser preview does not execute Swift.
content_blocks.troubleshooting: If compilation fails, check the exact diagnostic, toolchain version, imports, target platform and whether this snippet belongs in a package/test target rather than a standalone file.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the snippet from this lesson file, make one change at a time, and run the same check again.

content_blocks.title: Keep in mind
content_blocks.text: Use the compiler and versioned documentation as evidence. Do not treat a source-string check or an illustrative output as proof that a complete Swift program compiles on every platform.

content.task: Build a small Apple-platform design sketch or SwiftUI snippet for “Authentication and Identity”. Show the relevant view/state/service boundary and explain how keyboard access, accessibility labels, loading/error states, or localization should be checked.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming every Swift snippet can run in a browser or on every operating system.
common_mistakes.why: CodeLeaf’s current preview is not a Swift compiler, and Apple frameworks require appropriate target support.
common_mistakes.fix: Run command-line examples locally; use Xcode or a compatible package/target for framework-specific material.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating an illustrative output as compiler verification.
common_mistakes.why: A reference result helps reason about behavior but cannot replace compiling and testing the exact code.
common_mistakes.fix: Run the example with the stated toolchain and test one realistic edge case.

common_mistakes.why: Swift concurrency checks and newer APIs can vary by language mode and toolchain.
common_mistakes.fix: Read the exact diagnostic and confirm the supported version before changing safety checks.

summary: Authentication and Identity is part of the ordered Swift learning path.
Use the small example to make one rule concrete, then verify behavior and at least one boundary case.
For advanced and specialist topics, check the compiler version, platform support, and official release information.
content.solution_notes: Exercise reference answers remain in protected content files. The example output is illustrative until the snippet has been run in its intended environment.
content.run_instructions: Use a local Swift 6.4-compatible toolchain for command-line examples. SwiftUI and Apple-framework examples require an appropriate Apple SDK. In-app execution requires a separate isolated Swift runner, which is not included in this patch.
